# demosaic

Joint Bayer demosaicing and denoising in linear camera RGB, with physical noise
conditioning, frozen DINOv3 features and tiled 16-bit output on NVIDIA GB10.
**V120 Small is the general recommendation**: full 427-photo mean 37.04008 dB,
measured known/unseen-CFA means 54.31272/54.00872 dB, tested ADC maximum 55.52 DN16.
It uses a pretrained DRUNet trunk and the official DINOv3 ConvNeXt-Small pyramid.
[Primary results](docs/v120-v121-primary.md) · [Current choices](docs/current-model.md).

The [V174 spread-sampling experiment](docs/spread-sample-matching.md)
keeps wide matching positions but does not recover more fine fence crossings.
EMA quiet total RMS falls **0.12–0.17% versus V172**, with DC color error down
0.36–0.43%; mesh response slips **0.25% to 3.868% of exact constructed GT amplitude**.
Flat results are mixed and broad mottle persists. Both endpoints, all 822 cases,
60 actually viewed native figures and 133 CPU tests are complete. Keep V172 as
the balanced matching baseline for detail work. The separate six-input
[V175 path-removal probe](docs/results/v175-local-shortcut-diagnostic-v1.json)
finds a nonzero matching contribution; it does not establish why detail is lost.

The completed [V175 fresh-noise continuation](docs/fresh-noise-matching.md)
reaches 9,000 total updates but barely changes mesh response: **+0.03–0.05%
versus V172**, reaching 3.878–3.879% of exact constructed GT amplitude. Raw
quiet RMS falls **0.14–0.27%**, while EMA ISO12800 quiet RMS rises 0.21%.
Flat results remain mixed, broad mottle persists and real fine crossings stay
weak. Both endpoints, 822 cases and 60 actually viewed native figures are complete.

An [exact-template training diagnostic](docs/mesh-template-evidence.md) finds
much more conditional mesh evidence across larger areas. It supplies hidden GT
and makes no new model-quality or flat-safety claim.
A [CFA phase-split follow-up](docs/phase-frequency-evidence.md) tests whether
input-only frequency selections repeat in separately measured green samples.
The completed [V178 phase-evidence trial](docs/phase-evidence-comparison.md)
exposes those measurements to matching. Mesh response rises **0.92% over its
matched control**, reaching **3.924% of exact GT amplitude**. Quiet spatial
error rises slightly; broad mottle and real fine cab crossings remain unresolved.
All four endpoints, 72 actually viewed native figures and independent audits
are complete. Retain this small mesh-response option alongside the earlier strengths.
The completed [V180 local-window variant](docs/local-phase-evidence-comparison.md)
raises mesh response **15.2–15.9% over global V178**, reaching **4.52–4.55% of GT**
at the same parameter budget. Quiet spatial RMS rises **0.76–1.05%**, and actual
fine cab crossings remain incomplete. Both endpoints, independent audits and
60 actually viewed figures are complete. Retain this stronger detail architecture
alongside the earlier quiet and flat strengths.

The completed [V181 spatial-loss variant](docs/flat-spatial-evidence-comparison.md)
recovers quiet-field performance on the local architecture: EMA quiet spatial
RMS falls **0.47–1.15% versus V180 on all 32 inputs**. Mesh response falls
**8.75% to 4.150% of GT**, still 5.78% above global V178. Natural fine-band
response also falls; real cab crossings and broad mottle remain unresolved.
Retain this quieter option beside V180's stronger response and V172's balanced
comparison. Both endpoints, independent audits and 60 actually viewed figures
are complete.

A [training-gradient diagnostic](docs/flat-spatial-gradient-conflict.md) finds
that flat and paired-detail supervision can conflict through shared parameters,
despite positive output-gradient alignment. It changes no model or quality result.

| [V181 clean-flat spatial loss](docs/flat-spatial-evidence-comparison.md) | EMA quiet spatial RMS −0.47–1.15% on all 32 inputs versus V180; mesh response still 5.78% above global V178 | Mesh response −8.75% versus V180 to 4.150% of GT; fine-band response falls and real crossings/broad mottle remain |
| [V158 regional DC](docs/regional-dc-regret.md) | Quiet RMS −1.93–2.63% versus matched MSE; all 32 inputs improve | Small regressions versus V143, persistent real detail loss |

No model combines these strengths. The [released V170 RAW matching comparison](docs/nonlocal-raw-comparison.md)
has stronger coarse-flat reduction but periodic low-noise artifacts and weaker
mesh response. [Fine-mesh training](docs/fine-mesh-training.md) documents useful
finer-wire data gains and their quiet-field costs. Complete earlier strengths,
failures and evidence remain in [current choices](docs/current-model.md), the
[experiment index](docs/experiments.md) and [timestamped diary](diary/index.md).
Training uses freely licensed photos, geometry before downsampling and zero
optical blur. [Data pipeline](docs/training-pipeline.md) · [Source review](docs/current-source-loss-review.md).

## Setup and inference

Linux, Python 3.12+, `uv` and a CUDA 13-compatible NVIDIA driver are required for
the lockfile. DINOv3 requires approved Hugging Face access through `HF_TOKEN`.

```bash
source scripts/env.sh
uv sync --extra dev
uv run demosaic infer /mnt/external/demosaic/models/v120-final20000.pt photo.raf \
  /mnt/external/demosaic/output/photo-linear.tiff \
  --preview /mnt/external/demosaic/output/photo-srgb.tiff \
  --shot 0.001 --read 0.000001 \
  --tile 512 --overlap 64 --batch-size 4 --precision float32 --cudnn-benchmark
PYTHONPATH=.:src:scripts uv run pytest -q
```

`--phase-harmonic --phase-harmonic-envelope detail` restores contrast inside
reciprocal support. Use `cross` for lower tested blank RMS. The stage remains
opt-in, with `detail` its default; [tradeoffs and complete native comparisons](docs/supported-wave-amplitude.md).

Noise values are examples; use suitable camera/input priors.
Use `--phase-harmonic` to enable Detail, or
`--phase-harmonic --phase-harmonic-envelope edge` for the earlier stage.
[Usage and all explicit modes](docs/usage.md) retain the earlier comparisons.
[Linear DNG + full-resolution JPEG batch export](docs/dng-export.md) preserves
camera RGB and adapts existing darktable XMP edits. Add `--hot-pixels` to repair
isolated Bayer defects before restoration.
`--hot-pixel-clusters` also handles paired same-color defects; see the
[native crop investigation](docs/hot-pixel-clusters.md).

# Documentation guide

Start with [current model choices](current-model.md). **V120 Small remains the
general recommendation** with broad photo/camera and complete 102MP RGB16
checks. For fine dark detail and sky, compare [V172 local-noise matching](local-noise-matching.md),
the stronger [V161 detail prototype](harmonic-frequency-context.md),
[V171 standalone-flat strength](learned-matching-residual.md), and the
[V173](weak-gradient-matching.md)/[V174](spread-sample-matching.md) quiet gains.
Their remaining weaknesses differ; none combines strong mesh recovery and
clean quiet fields. The latest completed
[native-pixel viewer](images/v181-flat-spatial-evidence-v1/native-viewer.html) retains
both protected GFX scenes and the earlier useful comparators.

The completed [V180 local-evidence comparison](local-phase-evidence-comparison.md)
raises mesh response **15.2–15.9% over global V178**, reaching 4.52–4.55% of
constructed GT amplitude at the same parameter budget. Quiet spatial RMS rises
0.76–1.05%; fine cab crossings and broad/fine mottle remain unresolved.
Both endpoints, independent training/quality audits and all 60 native figures/
12 triplets are complete and actually inspected. Fifteen methods retain the
earlier detail, quiet and flat strengths.

The completed [V181 clean-flat spatial loss](flat-spatial-evidence-comparison.md)
reduces EMA quiet spatial RMS **0.47–1.15% versus V180 on all 32 inputs**, with
mesh response **−8.75% to 4.150% of GT**, still 5.78% above global V178. It
retains the architecture and old seven terms. Natural fine-band response falls,
broad mottle persists and real crossings remain weak. Retain the quieter recipe
alongside V180's stronger detail and earlier balanced/quiet/flat strengths.
Both endpoints/all 822 cases, full trace/five checkpoints, independent audits,
two strict exports and all 60 actually inspected native figures/12 triplets
are complete. [Loss implementation and preparation](flat-spatial-evidence.md).

The completed [V182 training-gradient diagnostic](flat-spatial-gradient-conflict.md)
finds negative flat/detail parameter-gradient cosines on 10/12 paired cases,
despite positive output cosines on all twelve. The added flat direction opposes
the measured target-pair response on 12/12 in a fixed saved-Adam metric.
All 20 native training batches and an independent audit are complete, with zero
optimizer updates. This guides the next loss experiment; V180/V181's actual
quality comparisons and the earlier useful models remain unchanged.

# Current method research

The completed [V180 local/global comparison](local-phase-evidence-comparison.md)
shows that spatially varying coefficient fields help mean mesh response:
**+15.23% raw / +15.93% EMA versus global V178**, reaching 4.52–4.55% of GT.
The same parameter budget and continuation recipe remain; windowed nuisance
fits, aggregation and interpolation change together. The gain is uneven,
and actual cab crossings still do not clearly recover. Quiet spatial RMS
increases 0.76–1.05% versus global V178; 31/32 EMA quiet inputs worsen.
Amplified native views show stronger fine texture over broad colored mottle.
Use this local-evidence architecture as the next detail-development baseline,
keeping V172's balanced and earlier quiet/flat strengths available. Controlling
the extra response in blank regions remains necessary. All 60 native figures
were inspected, and full training/checkpoint/quality audits pass.

The completed [V181 follow-up](flat-spatial-evidence-comparison.md) adds spatial-error variance inside
the existing 17px clean-flat mask, at fixed 4-DN16 units and weight 0.25. It
separates spatial pressure from constant RGB bias while retaining actual weak
target gradients. The architecture, original seven terms, mask and training
recipe are unchanged. All 55 focused CPU tests and two native CUDA updates with
genuine restoration pass; both loss and 6.29 million output-gradient coordinates
match CPU with zero observed differences. Matched training, full-trace/five-checkpoint
and quality audits, both endpoints/all 822 cases and actual inspection of all
60 native figures are complete. EMA quiet spatial RMS falls **0.47–1.15% on
all 32 inputs versus V180**, but mesh response falls **8.75% to 4.150% of GT**
and natural fine-band response falls on all 128 inputs. It retains 5.78% more
mean mesh response than global V178; quiet spatial changes versus V172 are
−0.058% / +0.283%. Clean-target masking does not prevent shared-parameter detail
suppression, and removing DC from the added term does not guarantee lower bias.
Retain this quieter local recipe and V180's stronger response as separate useful
options. Broad mottle and real fine crossings remain unresolved.
[Loss implementation and exact preparation](flat-spatial-evidence.md).

The completed [V182 local-gradient study](flat-spatial-gradient-conflict.md)
finds that the new spatial term conflicts with paired-difference loss in shared
parameters on 10/12 selected paired training cases. Output-gradient cosines
remain positive on all twelve. A negative added-spatial direction reduces the
full-target pair-response functional on 12/12 with a fixed saved-Adam denominator,
including within the shared network alone. This is local geometry, omitting
first/new second moments, clipping, decay and cross-batch effects; it predicts
no finite training or real-photo gain. All 20 native forwards, 76 parameter
backwards, independent array/loss/retained-gradient audit and actual plot viewing
are complete, with no updates or new data/noise. A coherent pair-response term
is the next experiment to prepare while retaining the absolute and flat losses.

The completed [V178 matched phase-evidence trial](phase-evidence-comparison.md)
raises constructed-mesh response **0.920% raw / 0.915% EMA over matched control**,
reaching 3.9243% / 3.9235% of GT amplitude. This is uneven: fewer than half of
the 256 paired inputs increase, while 201–209 increase against V172 EMA.
Quiet spatial error rises at both noise levels versus control; tiny total-error
gains largely reflect DC changes. Actual fine cab crossings do not clearly
recover, and contrast40 exposes broad colored mottle. All 72 native figures
were inspected; both full training traces/ten checkpoints and all four review
endpoints pass independent audits. The feature operator and 3,120 extra weights
change together, so their individual contributions are not isolated.
Retain the small mesh gain alongside earlier quiet/flat/detail strengths.
Spatially local coefficients are now measured in completed V180 above, with
unchanged global frequency selection and remaining support-spreading/seam risks.
The goal of strong fine dark detail with clean sky remains open.

The completed [V175 fresh-noise continuation](fresh-noise-matching.md) supplies
little additional fine-detail response after 8,100 more updates: mesh gain is
only 0.052% raw/0.033% EMA versus V172, with missing real cab crossings. Raw
quiet total RMS falls 0.135%/0.269% across ISO6400/12800 means, but 11/32 inputs
worsen and native512 ISO6400 full-flat RMS rises 0.091%. EMA ISO12800 quiet RMS
rises 0.213% as DC error increases despite lower spatial error. Photograph band
response falls slightly. All 60 native figures were actually inspected: broad
mottle and texture loss persist. Retain the small raw quiet gain and the earlier
detail/quiet/flat options. The completed audits cover all 9,000 continuation
rows, 8,100 loss totals, 141 Adam states at 9,000 and both endpoint reviews.
Longer fresh-noise training alone barely changes this tradeoff; the separate
V178 matched trial tests access to measured phase evidence, with results above.

The [V180 local-evidence variant](local-phase-evidence-matching.md) implements
local affine-projected coefficients at V178's globally selected frequencies,
with the same 3,120-weight adapter and matching parameter budget. Default
65-packed-pixel windows and 32-pixel stride follow the training-only support
diagnostic. All 112 focused CPU tests pass; six native cases match NumPy across
85,196,800 FP64 values, with maximum error 1.05e−12 and FP32 outputs equal to
FP64 casts. This CPU preparation is separate from restored quality. Interpolation
changes noise covariance and can spread support or create seams. Actual CUDA
initial parity, gradients and restoration now pass; CPU/GPU map differences
stay below 3e−8 and local-power differences below 7e−13. The 900-update continuation
from the same V172 Adam/EMA history and cached V178 recipe is complete, with
the detail/quiet tradeoff measured above.
The completed V178 workers retained their frozen recipe; V175's completed outcomes
remain separate.

The [local-phase support diagnostic](local-phase-support.md) reuses V177's fixed
primary bins and measures local affine-projected coefficients in the other
green phase. Across all 614 present observations, signal-containing mean power
rises 5.749→12.572→21.761 with larger boxes; blank means remain near 1, with
fewer blank contributors at the largest size. All 614 absent means remain near
1, yet roughly 1.7% of their windows exceed nominal power 4. This motivates
continuous spatial evidence without a hard gate. Twenty CPU tests and 288
native independent QR rows pass. It is training-input evidence, not restored
RGB or calibrated confidence; V175/V178 recipes and quality status stay unchanged.

V175's [first four continuation passes](fresh-noise-matching.md#four-pass-training-losses)
show only a 0.094% reduction in mesh pair-difference training loss; weak/photo
pair losses rise slightly. Standalone-flat anchor falls 0.558%, while photo
flat-anchor rises 4.797%. Noise, parameters and LR change together, and these
are moving-model training values rather than checkpoint quality. They supply
no basis to assume that longer training has already recovered more strands;
the final detail/flat/native outcomes are now available in the completed report above.

The completed [V178 matched continuation](phase-evidence-training.md) compares one
additional cached pass at the same raw/Adam/EMA starting point and budget.
The existing 141 optimizer clocks continue from 900; the new adapter starts from 0
and is included in EMA and restoration. Thirteen CPU state tests and actual
checkpoint checks pass, followed by actual training/quality audits and all
72 original-detail native figures. Both old network clocks finish at 1,800;
the evidence adapter clock finishes at 900. Labeled baseline fixtures remain
separate from actual scores/pixels and cannot pass actual publication gates.

The [V178 native CUDA admission](phase-evidence-admission.md) has passed after
V175's complete GPU pipeline. All 14 zero-adapter RGB comparisons are bit-exact;
CPU/CUDA features differ by at most 2.00e−6 within fixed tolerance. Both probe
updates have nonzero gradients on all 142 tensors, exact model/Adam/RNG
restoration and post-update ADC/mixed-zero invariants. Peak allocation is
6.27 GiB. The earlier 18 CPU protocol tests and dependency rejection remain
preserved. These checks establish execution; the separate trained-quality
comparison is complete above.

The [V178 phase-evidence matching path](phase-evidence-matching.md) makes the
V177 observations available to the matching network as continuous features.

cross/frequency maps; a zero 3,120-weight projection adds them to the existing
39 matching coordinates. This differs from another spectral descriptor in the
already frozen component: the matching branch can directly use the measured
waves while learning spatial support. It introduces no hard detection threshold
or direct sinusoid-to-RGB correction. All 68 CPU checks and native feature/strict

and noisy-field costs above; completed V175 results remain separate.

The [V177 within-image CFA sample split](phase-frequency-evidence.md) closes a
specific diagnostic gap: one green RAW phase selects an unknown frequency and
the other measures it, with GT entering only afterward. Primary nominal power≥16
occurs in 170/614 present and 0/614 matched absent training cases. At≥4, six
absent cases pass; considering eight candidates raises that to 71. This suggests
using continuous repeatability evidence, with no calibrated detector or safe
restoration claim. A strict power16 gate misses 204/374 cases whose V176
conditional green SNR is≥5, and negative principal-band agreement occurs on
reference-supported peaks. Native aliases, spatial support and weak evidence
must be preserved rather than treating one signed spectral statistic as truth.
All 33 CPU checks and independent QR/DFT verification pass; no model is trained.

The [V176 training-template diagnostic](mesh-template-evidence.md) measures
conditional evidence in all 614 retained noisy mesh pairs. Green median
known-template SNR rises from 0.653 in the best native16 window to 7.360 over
native512; all-CFA medians rise from 0.893 to 10.502. Small-window evidence is
often weak even with an exact template. This motivates investigating useful
aggregation over larger areas, but hidden template/background/variances are
supplied. It proves neither inference recoverability nor flat safety, and does
not measure the existing model's receptive field. V143's matched training
Bayer-sample amplitudes also remain weak on many high-conditional-SNR cases;

training recipe at V172's unchanged model and seven-term objective. It starts
from the actual raw/Adam/EMA states, adds 8,100 updates and regenerates physical

photo rows per pass retain their original observations/parents rather than
substitute a clipped target for clean sensor data. The full 1,000-row preflight
and 54 focused tests pass. Its budget, fresh realizations and reheated learning
rate change together; individual effects are not isolated. Training has
completed with the small quiet gain and costs reported above; V172 remains
the balanced matching baseline.

The final comparison now includes all 822 saved V161 EMA outputs, re-reduced on
identical inputs/parents/ROIs and current metric bytes. All 8,038 comparable old

**Mesh response falls 3.95% to 3.724% of GT**; natural fine-band response falls

## Current hypotheses and evidence

establish flat safety: an exact zero-DC kernel can amplify white-noise variance
by9/8, and nonnegative spatial gating after filtering can introduce DC. Zero
whole-image mean also permits local quiet-region shifts. The current spectral
proposal is spatially gated after its band restriction; future changes must
check delivered camera RGB, local bias and noise. These are algebra
counterexamples, not trained-model performance or a rejection of RIECR.

(682 pairs). Among 614 noisy pairs, 202 of 1,228 carrier families have center
periods inside the real reference's dominant 7.12–9.40 pixel interval, but only
13 pairs have both families there. The generator spans nominal 6–32 pixel
periods; projective geometry broadens the observed local period range. The
audit accounts for its Jacobian at five locations rather than treating the
nominal recipe as the final frequency. These are analytic carrier estimates,
not measured peaks after masking, interpolation and area reduction.

(10th–90th percentiles 0.374–15.66); 264/614 are below 2 DN16 RMS and 47/614
even have peak differences below 2 DN16. Median full-context signal/input-noise
RMS ratio is 0.00932. That energy proxy does not measure matched-filter
detectability or restored RGB error. The 68 ADC-only pairs are reported
separately. This suggests testing stronger coverage of fine crossed carriers
across an explicit contrast/noise ladder, with matched empty controls. Simply
lowering contrast would make many already weak examples weaker. This is a
data hypothesis, not an established explanation or quality gain; V167 remains

## Native frequencies from packed phases

[DFENet](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.15800v1), with a November2026 journal issue
and March2025 preprint, separates spatial detail refinement from CFA-guided
frequency suppression. Sections3–5 describe staged RGB/spectral supervision,
Gaussian CFA-noise tests, synthetic line patterns and local patch inference.
Those results do not establish physical shot/read-noise behavior or our sky/fence
quality. No paper implementation, weights or dataset are adopted.

Our eight deterministic scalar-mosaic fixtures distinguish invertible packing
from averaging. All four phase spectra, combined with their native phase factors,
reconstruct every full-resolution mosaic Fourier bin: maximum difference
4.33e−17 versus FFT and 5.93e−16 versus an independent dense DFT. Pack/unpack
is bit-exact. Two native frequencies, +0.125 and −0.375 cycles/pixel, have identical
even-x phase samples and matching per-phase spectral magnitudes after DC removal,
but different cross-phase signs. The complete packed tuple distinguishes them.

Our inference is that explicit native-alias features could make available phase
relationships easier to learn. Packing itself does not discard recorded RAW
samples; dropping phase, mixing phases or restricting bands can discard distinctions.
This algebra does not reconstruct unmeasured RGB samples, measure trained detail
recovery or establish flat safety. V166's fixed common-support routing trial is
unchanged. [Own fixtures, source and primary-paper record](results/packed-fourier-reading-20261107-v1.json).

The July2026 [WGCAN publisher abstract](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0262885626002441)
describes wavelet low/high processing followed by color reconstruction. The full
publisher page returned403; the abstract and author code were reviewed separately.

the wavelet term sums mean L1 differences over all four one-level Haar bands,
including LL. Training uses RAW/RGB/wavelet weights0.7/0.2/0.1 after RGB clipping;
the reported validation loss uses0.5/0.4/0.1. A helper's Euclidean name does not
describe its actual L1 operation.

Our inference is to specify the exact transform, normalization and subband
weighting before interpreting any wavelet-loss comparison. This paired-exposure
RAW/RGB pipeline does not establish our physical-noise-conditioned camera-RGB
or quiet-sky quality. The inspected repository declares no license; no code,
weights or data are adopted. V166 remains fixed. [Primary URLs, pinned file hashes,
line references and reading limits](results/wgcan-reading-20261107-v1.json).

# Why flat supervision can suppress paired detail

**V182 finds a local conflict through shared neural parameters.** The added
spatial loss and paired-detail loss have positive output-gradient cosines on
all 12 paired training cases. Their parameter-gradient cosines are negative
on 10/12, in both Euclidean coordinates and a fixed saved-Adam denominator
metric. In that fixed metric, a negative spatial-gradient direction decreases
the measured target-pair response on **all 12 cases**, including at the completed
V181 state. The shared matching network alone has the same 12/12 response sign;
the evidence adapter alone has 10/12. This supports investigating coherent
pair-response supervision while retaining the flat penalties.

These are local training derivatives, **not a new trained model or a measured
quality gain**. [V181's actual comparison](flat-spatial-evidence-comparison.md)
remains authoritative: quieter fields cost mesh and photographic response;
real fine cab crossings and broad colored mottle remain unresolved. The local
architecture remains useful, with both quieter V181 and stronger-response V180
recipes retained alongside earlier strengths. V120 Small remains the general
recommendation.

applies to **both parameter plots**; the right panel uses a logarithmic ratio axis.

## Fixed training-only measurements

Two completed raw checkpoints, V180 and V181, each see the same ten cached
four-image batches. Selection is fixed before any forward: the first and middle
noisy batch in each of mesh, weak texture, photo, mixed structure and flat
domains. Actual row numbers are 1/505, 5/433, 2/478, 4/529 and 8/553 respectively.
These use the existing cached sources, counterfactuals, physical noise, parent
predictions and pair units. No protected GFX input enters this diagnostic.

Five scalar functionals are differentiated: the original weighted seven-term
total, the weighted V181 spatial addition, weighted paired-difference and common
losses, and mean normalized target-pair response. Response is the projection of
the restored pair difference onto its actual clean difference, divided by that
pair's own target energy, then averaged over pairs. It is a **full-target response,
not a frequency-band score**. The six unique paired targets have DC energy
fractions below 7e−11, so constant RGB differences account for negligible target
energy here. This still does not identify a particular missing fine orientation.

For scalar gradients g and h, ordinary parameter products are gᵀh. The second
metric is gᵀDh, with positive diagonal
`D = 1 / (sqrt(saved_v / (1 − beta2^step)) + epsilon)` in FP64. Saved network
clocks are 1,800 and adapter clocks 900. This fixes the denominator at the saved
state; it omits first moments, the next second-moment update, clipping, decay,
finite steps and cross-batch interactions. It is **not an actual AdamW update**.
No gradient projection or optimizer change is justified by a cosine alone.
